title: Claude Model History
content:
## Overview

Claude is Anthropic's family of AI assistants, first released in early 2023. Each generation has brought meaningful jumps in capability, context length, and cost-efficiency. This page tracks the major releases and what changed with each one.

---

## Claude 1 (March 2023)

The first publicly available Claude, launched via API and the Claude.ai interface. Introduced Anthropic's "Constitutional AI" approach to alignment — training the model to critique and revise its own outputs against a set of principles rather than relying solely on human feedback (RLHF).

**Key specs:** ~9K token context window, text-only input.

---

## Claude 2 (July 2023)

A major capability jump. Notable improvements in coding, math, and instruction following. Introduced a **100K token context window** — at the time one of the largest available, enabling entire codebases or books to fit in a single prompt.

**Key specs:** 100K context, text-only input, improved reasoning benchmarks.

---

## Claude 2.1 (November 2023)

Expanded context to **200K tokens** and significantly reduced hallucination rates on long-document tasks. Also introduced system prompt support and improved tool use.

---

## Claude 3 Family (March 2024)

Anthropic introduced a three-tier model family with a consistent naming convention that persists today:

- **Haiku** — fastest, cheapest, suitable for high-throughput applications
- **Sonnet** — balanced capability and cost, the default workhorse
- **Opus** — most capable, used for complex reasoning tasks

All Claude 3 models gained **vision (image input)** support, enabling document analysis, chart reading, and screenshot processing. Context window: 200K tokens across all tiers.

**Claude 3 Opus** set new benchmarks on MMLU, HumanEval, and GSM8K at launch.

---

## Claude 3.5 Sonnet (June 2024)

A landmark release: **Claude 3.5 Sonnet outperformed Claude 3 Opus on most benchmarks while being significantly faster and cheaper**. This broke the usual pattern where the top-tier model leads on capability.

Also introduced **Artifacts** in Claude.ai — the ability to generate self-contained code, documents, and interactive apps displayed in a side panel.

---

## Claude 3.5 Sonnet v2 / Computer Use (October 2024)

Updated Claude 3.5 Sonnet with improved coding and a major new capability: **computer use (beta)** — the ability to control a computer by seeing the screen and issuing mouse/keyboard actions. Made available via API for developers to build agentic desktop automation.

---

## Claude 3.5 Haiku (November 2024)

The fastest and most affordable Claude 3.5 model. Matched or exceeded Claude 3 Opus on several benchmarks despite being positioned as the lightweight tier.

---

## Claude 4 Family (2025)

The Haiku / Sonnet / Opus naming continued through the Claude 4.x line. Key model IDs (superseded by the releases below as of mid-2026):

| Model | ID | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Haiku 4.5 | `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` | Fastest/cheapest Claude 4, still current for lightweight workloads |
| Sonnet 4.5 | `claude-sonnet-4-5` | Balanced |
| Sonnet 4.6 | `claude-sonnet-4-6` | Released Feb 2026; superseded as default by Sonnet 5 |
| Opus 4.7 | `claude-opus-4-7` | Superseded by Opus 4.8 |

Claude 4 models show substantial improvements in agentic task completion, long multi-turn coherence, and instruction following precision.

---

## Claude Opus 4.8 (May 28, 2026)

An incremental but well-regarded update to Opus 4.7, available via `claude-opus-4-8` on claude.ai, Claude Code, and the API. Fixes the comment-verbosity and tool-calling regressions reported in 4.7 and adds:

- **Improved honesty/error detection** — roughly 4x less likely than 4.7 to let flaws in its own generated code pass unremarked; more willing to flag its own uncertainty.
- **69.2% on SWE-bench Pro** at launch, ahead of GPT-5.5 and Gemini 3.1 Pro on the same benchmark.
- **Dynamic workflows (research preview)** — Claude plans a large task and then runs hundreds of parallel subagents within a single Claude Code session to execute it.
- **Fast mode** — 2.5x faster, priced at $10/$50 per million input/output tokens (vs. $5/$25 for standard); standard pricing is unchanged from 4.7.

---

## Claude Fable 5 & Claude Mythos 5 (June 9, 2026)

Anthropic's first publicly available **Mythos-class** models — a new capability tier above the Haiku/Sonnet/Opus line. Fable 5 is the general-access version; Mythos 5 is the same underlying model with some safeguards lifted, offered only to a vetted group of cyberdefenders and infrastructure providers.

- State-of-the-art at launch on nearly all tracked capability benchmarks: software engineering, knowledge work, vision, and scientific research.
- Can work autonomously for longer stretches than any prior Claude model. Stripe reported Fable 5 completed a codebase-wide migration in a day that would otherwise have taken a full team over two months.
- Ships with topic-based safeguards: queries that trip certain safety triggers are silently routed to Claude Opus 4.8 instead of Fable 5. This triggers in under 5% of sessions on average.
- Available on the Claude API, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Foundry at $10 per million input tokens / $50 per million output tokens.
- Model ID: `claude-fable-5`. Anthropic has since extended general access to Fable 5 more than once (most recently mid-July 2026) in response to competing frontier-model launches from OpenAI.

---

## Claude Sonnet 5 (June 30, 2026)

Positioned as Anthropic's most agentic Sonnet yet, and the new default model for Free and Pro plans (also available on Max, Team, and Enterprise). Model ID: `claude-sonnet-5`.

- **1M token context window** — this is both the default and the maximum; there is no smaller-context variant, unlike earlier Sonnet releases.
- **128K max output tokens**, plus adaptive (variable-depth) extended thinking.
- Meaningful gains over Sonnet 4.6 on agentic reasoning, tool use, coding, and knowledge-work benchmarks.
- New tokenizer produces roughly 30% more tokens for the same input text than Sonnet 4.6's tokenizer, so per-request cost can rise even though per-token pricing is flat.
- Introductory pricing of $2/$10 per million input/output tokens runs through August 31, 2026, after which it reverts to standard $3/$15 pricing.

---

## Current Model Lineup (as of July 2026)

| Model | ID | Tier |
|---|---|---|
| Haiku 4.5 | `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` | Fast/cheap |
| Sonnet 5 | `claude-sonnet-5` | Default balanced tier |
| Opus 4.8 | `claude-opus-4-8` | Most capable of the standard tiers |
| Fable 5 | `claude-fable-5` | Mythos-class, frontier capability, premium pricing |

---

## Key Trends Across Generations

- **Context window:** 9K → 100K → 200K → 1M tokens (Sonnet 5, June 2026)
- **Multimodal:** Text-only → Vision → Computer use
- **Tier structure:** Single model → Three tiers (Haiku / Sonnet / Opus) → Four tiers with the addition of Mythos-class models (Fable 5 / Mythos 5)
- **Cost curve:** Each generation brings the previous generation's top-tier capability down to mid-tier pricing
- **Agentic focus:** Increasing emphasis on tool use, long-horizon tasks, and integration with external systems; Opus 4.8's dynamic workflows extend this to hundreds of parallel subagents in a single session
